parakeet: The Abrahamic religion tells us that God is like a loving father who deeply desires connections with his children. But what kind of father hides from his kids? If your earthly father ignored your calls, never showed up when you needed him, and refused to acknowledge you, would you still believe that he loved you? But when God does it, you're told he's testing your faith. You're told, just wait, he'll show up in his own time. You told you just have to believe harder. But at what point do you stop making excuses for someone who never shows up? Because if an all-powerful, all-loving God actually wanted to be known, wouldn't he just make himself known? Wouldn't he communicate clearly, directly, and unmistakably? Instead, believers spend their entire lives chasing a feeling, second guessing themselves, wondering if God is speaking or if it's just their own thoughts. Spoiler alert, it's just your own thoughts. And at some point, you have to ask yourself, is God really there? Or have we just been trained to interpret silence as presence? Because if God's greatest desire is for us to know him, why does he make it feel impossible? Why do miracles only seem to happen in ways that can't be tested? People claim them all the time: God healed my headache, God helped me find my car keys, God made sure I got that promotion. But let me ask you something.
